Some examples of memory reference instructions: Transfers the contents of the memory location labeled COUNT into accumulator 1.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: This was the standard method for making an _____ system call on early Nova models; the assembly language mnemonic .SYSTM translated to this
Data General Nova.fact: This was the standard method for making an RDOS system call on early Nova models; the assembly language mnemonic .SYSTM translated to this.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Decrement the value in the location labeled _____, and skip the next instruction if the result is zero
Data General Nova.fact: Decrement the value in the location labeled COUNT, and skip the next instruction if the result is zero.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: INTDS — disabled all interrupts _____ — enabled all interrupts IORST — I/O reset
Data General Nova.fact: INTDS — disabled all interrupts INTEN — enabled all interrupts IORST — I/O reset.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The interrupt handler would then perform an _____ instruction to discover the channel number of the interrupting device
Data General Nova.fact: The interrupt handler would then perform an INTA instruction to discover the channel number of the interrupting device.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: There were a few devices, notably the CPU's power-failure detection circuit, which did not respond to the _____ instruction
Data General Nova.fact: There were a few devices, notably the CPU's power-failure detection circuit, which did not respond to the INTA instruction. If the INTA returned a result of zero, the interrupt service routine had to poll all of the non-INTA-responding devices using the SKPDZ/SKPDN instructions to see which one interrupted.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: If the _____ returned a result of zero, the interrupt service routine had to poll all of the non-INTA-responding devices using the SKPDZ/SKPDN instructions to see which one interrupted
Data General Nova.fact: There were a few devices, notably the CPU's power-failure detection circuit, which did not respond to the INTA instruction. If the INTA returned a result of zero, the interrupt service routine had to poll all of the non-INTA-responding devices using the SKPDZ/SKPDN instructions to see which one interrupted.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: When _____ was executed, interrupts would not be enabled until after the following instruction was executed; that instruction was expected to be the JMP@ 0 instruction
Data General Nova.fact: In order to prevent a pending interrupt from interrupting immediately before the return jump (which would cause the return address to be overwritten), the INTEN instruction had a one-instruction-cycle delay. When INTEN was executed, interrupts would not be enabled until after the following instruction was executed; that instruction was expected to be the JMP@ 0 instruction.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The operating system could somewhat manage the ordering of interrupts by setting an interrupt mask using the _____ instruction
Data General Nova.fact: The operating system could somewhat manage the ordering of interrupts by setting an interrupt mask using the MSKO instruction.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: This was enough time to stop I/O in progress, by issuing an _____ instruction, and then save the contents of the four accumulators and the carry bit to memory
Data General Nova.fact: This was enough time to stop I/O in progress, by issuing an IORST instruction, and then save the contents of the four accumulators and the carry bit to memory.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: When the power returned, if the CPU's front panel key switch was in the _____ position, the CPU would start and perform an indirect jump through memory address 2
Data General Nova.fact: When the power returned, if the CPU's front panel key switch was in the LOCK position, the CPU would start and perform an indirect jump through memory address 2.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The data switches provided input to the CPU for various functions, and could also be read by a running program using the _____ assembly language instruction
Data General Nova.fact: The data switches provided input to the CPU for various functions, and could also be read by a running program using the READS assembly language instruction.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Referencing the Nova _____ photo, the first four switches from the left performed the EXAMINE and DEPOSIT functions for the four accumulators
Data General Nova.fact: Referencing the Nova 840 photo, the first four switches from the left performed the EXAMINE and DEPOSIT functions for the four accumulators.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Going to the right, the next switch was the _____/STOP switch
Data General Nova.fact: Going to the right, the next switch was the RESET/STOP switch. Pressing RESET caused the CPU to halt immediately, cleared a number of CPU internal registers, and sent an I/O reset signal to all connected devices.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Pressing _____ caused the CPU to halt immediately, cleared a number of CPU internal registers, and sent an I/O reset signal to all connected devices
Data General Nova.fact: Going to the right, the next switch was the RESET/STOP switch. Pressing RESET caused the CPU to halt immediately, cleared a number of CPU internal registers, and sent an I/O reset signal to all connected devices.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Pressing _____ caused the CPU to halt after completing the current instruction
Data General Nova.fact: Going to the right, the next switch was the RESET/STOP switch. Pressing STOP caused the CPU to halt after completing the current instruction.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The switch to the right of that was the _____/CONTINUE switch
Data General Nova.fact: The switch to the right of that was the START/CONTINUE switch. Pressing START transferred the value currently set in data switches 1–15 to the program counter, and then began executing from there.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Pressing _____ transferred the value currently set in data switches 1–15 to the program counter, and then began executing from there
Data General Nova.fact: The switch to the right of that was the START/CONTINUE switch. Pressing START transferred the value currently set in data switches 1–15 to the program counter, and then began executing from there.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The _____ STEP function caused the CPU to execute one instruction, at the current program counter location, and then halt
Data General Nova.fact: The INST STEP function caused the CPU to execute one instruction, at the current program counter location, and then halt. Since the program counter would be incremented as part of the instruction execution, this allowed the user to single-step through a program.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: MEMORY _____, a misnomer, caused the CPU to run through a single clock cycle and halt
Data General Nova.fact: The INST STEP function caused the CPU to execute one instruction, at the current program counter location, and then halt. Since the program counter would be incremented as part of the instruction execution, this allowed the user to single-step through a program.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: PROGRAM _____ was the mechanism usually used to boot a Nova
Data General Nova.fact: PROGRAM LOAD was the mechanism usually used to boot a Nova.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: When this switch was triggered, it caused the _____-word boot ROM to be mapped over the first 32 words of memory, set the program counter to 0, and started the CPU
Data General Nova.fact: When this switch was triggered, it caused the 32-word boot ROM to be mapped over the first 32 words of memory, set the program counter to 0, and started the CPU.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: They had to be repositioned to cylinder _____, where RDOS wrote the first-level boot block, in order for the boot sequence to work
Data General Nova.fact: If switch 0 was on, the boot ROM assumed the device was a DMA-capable device and it initiated a DMA data transfer. They had to be repositioned to cylinder 0, where RDOS wrote the first-level boot block, in order for the boot sequence to work.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The power switch was a 3-way keyed switch with positions marked OFF, ON, and _____
Data General Nova.fact: They had to be repositioned to cylinder 0, where RDOS wrote the first-level boot block, in order for the boot sequence to work. The power switch was a 3-way keyed switch with positions marked OFF, ON, and LOCK.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: However, unlike current CPUs, the CPU did not start automatically when power was applied; the user had to use PROGRAM _____ or some other method to start the CPU and initiate the boot sequence
Data General Nova.fact: However, unlike current CPUs, the CPU did not start automatically when power was applied; the user had to use PROGRAM LOAD or some other method to start the CPU and initiate the boot sequence.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Turning the switch to _____ disabled the front panel function switches; by turning the switch to LOCK and removing the key, the user could render the CPU resistant to tampering
Data General Nova.fact: Turning the switch to LOCK disabled the front panel function switches; by turning the switch to LOCK and removing the key, the user could render the CPU resistant to tampering. On systems with magnetic core memory, the LOCK position also enabled the auto power failure recovery function.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: On systems with magnetic core memory, the _____ position also enabled the auto power failure recovery function
Data General Nova.fact: Turning the switch to LOCK disabled the front panel function switches; by turning the switch to LOCK and removing the key, the user could render the CPU resistant to tampering. On systems with magnetic core memory, the LOCK position also enabled the auto power failure recovery function.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The key could be removed in the OFF or _____ positions
Data General Nova.fact: Turning the switch to LOCK disabled the front panel function switches; by turning the switch to LOCK and removing the key, the user could render the CPU resistant to tampering. On systems with magnetic core memory, the LOCK position also enabled the auto power failure recovery function.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: On the later _____ MV/6000, LDA and STA took 0.44 μs, ADD, etc
Data General Nova.fact: On the later Eclipse MV/6000, LDA and STA took 0.44 μs, ADD, etc.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: took 0.33 μs, MUL 2.2 μs, DIV 3.19 μs, ISZ 1.32 μs, FAD 5.17 μs, _____ 11.66 μs
Data General Nova.fact: took 0.33 μs, MUL 2.2 μs, DIV 3.19 μs, ISZ 1.32 μs, FAD 5.17 μs, FMMD 11.66 μs.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: It is designed to run under _____ and prints the string “Hello, world.” on the console
Data General Nova.fact: It is designed to run under RDOS and prints the string “Hello, world.” on the console.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Because the _____ .systm call macro implements a jsr, AC3 is overwritten by the return address for the .pchar function
Data General Nova.fact: Because the RDOS .systm call macro implements a jsr, AC3 is overwritten by the return address for the .pchar function.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: Sales accelerated as newer versions were introduced, and by 1975 the company had annual sales of US$_____
Data General Nova.fact: Sales accelerated as newer versions were introduced, and by 1975 the company had annual sales of US$100 million.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The resulting machine, known as the _____NOVA, was released in 1970
Data General Nova.fact: The resulting machine, called the SuperNOVA, was released in 1970. This was introduced later the same year as the SuperNOVA SC, featuring semiconductor (SC) memory.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The development of the MV-series was documented in _____'s popular 1981 book, The Soul of a New Machine
Data General Nova.fact: The development of the MV-series was documented in Tracy Kidder's popular 1981 book, The Soul of a New Machine.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: In spring 1970 they hired a new designer, _____, to leapfrog any possible machine in the making
Data General Nova.fact: In spring 1970 they hired a new designer, Larry Seligman, to leapfrog any possible machine in the making.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: The Nova 1200 also processed math serially in 4-bit packets, using a single 74181 ALU; the Nova 800 was a repackaged _____Nova
Data General Nova.fact: A year after its introduction, the SuperNova included a full 16-bit bitsliced parallel adder using four Signetics 8260 ICs. The Nova 1200 also processed math serially in 4-bit packets, using a single 74181 ALU; the Nova 800 was a repackaged SuperNova.

Data General Nova.subject: Applied Sciences
Data General Nova.question: They had to be repositioned to cylinder 0, where _____ wrote the first-level boot block, in order for the boot sequence to work
Data General Nova.fact: They had to be repositioned to cylinder 0, where RDOS wrote the first-level boot block, in order for the boot sequence to work.

Database engine.subject: Applied Sciences
Database engine.question: The _____ was Component of a database management system.
Database engine.fact: A database engine (or storage engine) is the underlying software component that a database management system (DBMS) uses to create, read, update and delete (CRUD) data from a database. The term "database engine" is frequently used interchangeably with "database server" or "database management system".

Database engine.subject: Applied Sciences
Database engine.question: For example, MySQL supports _____DB as well as MyISAM
Database engine.fact: For example, MySQL supports InnoDB as well as MyISAM.

Database engine.subject: Applied Sciences
Database engine.question: An operating _____ always utilizes several storage types simultaneously
Database engine.fact: An operating DBMS always utilizes several storage types simultaneously.

Database engine.subject: Applied Sciences
Database engine.question: Inside of a contemporary computer hosting a _____, most of the "database" part resides, partially replicated, in volatile storage
Database engine.fact: Inside of a contemporary computer hosting a DBMS, most of the "database" part resides, partially replicated, in volatile storage.

Database engine.subject: Applied Sciences
Database engine.question: A fast cache, typically consisting of volatile and fast _____, is connected (via standard interfaces) to drives
Database engine.fact: A fast cache, typically consisting of volatile and fast DRAM, is connected (via standard interfaces) to drives.

Database engine.subject: Applied Sciences
Database engine.question: A data structure type is selected upon _____ development to best meet the operations needed for the types of data it contains
Database engine.fact: A data structure type is selected upon DBMS development to best meet the operations needed for the types of data it contains. In some DBMSs database administrators have the flexibility to select among options of data structures to contain user data for performance reasons.

Database transaction.subject: Applied Sciences
Database transaction.question: The _____ was Unit of work performed within a database management system.
Database transaction.fact: A database transaction symbolizes a unit of work, performed within a database management system (or similar system) against a database, that is treated in a coherent and reliable way independent of other transactions.

Database transaction.subject: Applied Sciences
Database transaction.question: A distributed transaction enforces the _____ properties over multiple nodes, and might include systems such as databases, storage managers, file systems, messaging systems, and other data managers
Database transaction.fact: A distributed transaction enforces the ACID properties over multiple nodes, and might include systems such as databases, storage managers, file systems, messaging systems, and other data managers.

Database transaction.subject: Applied Sciences
Database transaction.question: There is occurring research into more data coherent filesystems, such as the _____ (WTF)
Database transaction.fact: There is occurring research into more data coherent filesystems, such as the Warp Transactional Filesystem (WTF).

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: The _____ was Database software.
Database Workbench.fact: Database Workbench is a software application for development and administration of multiple relational databases using SQL, with interoperationality between different database systems, developed by Upscene Productions. The main developer of Database Workbench, Martijn Tonies, was closely involved in the early development of Firebird, has been a committee member of the Firebird Foundation and continues to be a Foundation member and sponsor.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: During its early years, InterBase became open-source for a short while, and soon after _____ was created as a fork from the InterBase code base
Database Workbench.fact: During its early years, InterBase became open-source for a short while, and soon after Firebird was created as a fork from the InterBase code base. The main developer of Database Workbench, Martijn Tonies, was closely involved in the early development of Firebird, has been a committee member of the Firebird Foundation and continues to be a Foundation member and sponsor.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: Not long after, the program became interoperational between the different database systems and this initial support for multiple database systems led to the renaming of the product to its current titl
Database Workbench.fact: Not long after, the program became interoperational between the different database systems and this initial support for multiple database systems led to the renaming of the product to its current title "Database Workbench" in 2003. It also opened the path to the inclusion of support for more database systems: support for Microsoft SQL Server and MySQL was added in 2003; in 2005, support for Oracle Database and NexusDB was added and SQL Anywhere support followed in 2008.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: Early _____, a full Unicode version of Database Workbench was released and version 5 of Database Workbench was released in August 2014
Database Workbench.fact: Early 2010, a full Unicode version of Database Workbench was released and version 5 of Database Workbench was released in August 2014.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: In December _____, Database Workbench 6 was released with a revamped user interface including a more consistent look and feel and the multi-threaded loading of database metadata
Database Workbench.fact: In December 2021, Database Workbench 6 was released with a revamped user interface including a more consistent look and feel and the multi-threaded loading of database metadata.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: This version introduced the _____ with its TeamServer component
Database Workbench.fact: This version introduced the Enterprise Edition with its TeamServer component.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: Database Workbench 7 was released in July _____, adding AI features, dark mode, additional data import and export features and many use interface improvements
Database Workbench.fact: Database Workbench 7 was released in July 2026, adding AI features, dark mode, additional data import and export features and many use interface improvements.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: Inter_____ works with both Firebird and InterBase
Database Workbench.fact: Database Workbench 7 was released in July 2026, adding AI features, dark mode, additional data import and export features and many use interface improvements. A free version for personal use with limited functionality, Database Workbench Lite, is available for MySQL and Firebird.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: Version 2: _____, renamed to Database Workbench with modular approach for supported database systems, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle and NexusDB support added
Database Workbench.fact: Version 2: 2003, renamed to Database Workbench with modular approach for supported database systems, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle and NexusDB support added.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: Version 5: _____, High DPI aware and support for PostgreSQL added
Database Workbench.fact: Version 5: 2014, High DPI aware and support for PostgreSQL added.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: Version 6: _____, Enterprise Edition added, a special multi-user version with central repository of servers, databases and workspaces and a database Version Control System
Database Workbench.fact: Version 6: 2021, Enterprise Edition added, a special multi-user version with central repository of servers, databases and workspaces and a database Version Control System.

Database Workbench.subject: Applied Sciences
Database Workbench.question: Version 7.0: _____, AI features, dark mode, many user interface improvements
Database Workbench.fact: Version 7.0: 2026, AI features, dark mode, many user interface improvements.
